title: worktree merge: honor uat_stop, invert the post-merge lane write, hold the worktree
action: The merge side of CONTEXT.md D4.1, D4.2, D4.3. Locate every anchor BY NAME, not by line number — usp-1 already edited phases.rs and the numbers have shifted. (1) D4.1 — the merge-time uat precondition (the block that refuses WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_PENDING, today gated on uat_before_merge_config) now asks crate::uat::uat_stop_config. It refuses ONLY under UatStop::Merge; under Close and Off it does not refuse. A None from the reader keeps refusing the whole merge as an invalid-config error — keep the existing WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_CONFIG_INVALID code and widen its message to name BOTH keys and their legal values. Delete uat_before_merge_config from phases.rs once nothing calls it; its read now lives inside uat_stop_config. Keep --skip-uat working exactly as today under Merge. (2) D4.2 — close_the_lane_on_merge branches on the same resolved UatStop. Under Merge and Off, today's behavior is kept BYTE-FOR-BYTE: clear the waiting_on/run_state pair via clear_lane_waiting_on_pair and write the existing next_action naming bee close. Under Close, ask whether this feature's uat is still pending — reuse the same gate read the merge precondition uses (the live workflow record first, the default state record only as a same-feature fallback) and the lane rule crate::uat::uat_gate_applies_to_lane. If the lane cares AND uat is unapproved, do the INVERSE of today: set waiting_on kind gate, subject 'uat: <feature>', on the lane record, and write a next_action that names the road in one line — reload the product, test it, then either approve uat with bee gate --name uat --approved true, or fix in the worktree and merge again. If the lane is exempt, or uat is already approved, today's clear-and-point-at-close behavior is correct and stays. (3) D4.3 — while that uat wait is live, cleanup is forced OFF: --cleanup and config worktree_cleanup_on_merge true are both ignored, and the merge result carries one visible line saying why (the worktree is the only place a failed uat can be fixed; tearing it down drops the grant and the second merge would hit the no-granted-worktree refusal in handlers.rs). resolve_cleanup_on_merge in handlers.rs is the seam. --no-cleanup already means keep and is unaffected. (4) Preserve, and assert in tests, everything CONTEXT.md D5 says does not move: a merge NEVER writes lane phase; the lane write stays best-effort warn-never-fail (a failure warns, the merge stays green); ALREADY_UP_TO_DATE writes no lane change; MERGE_CONFLICT and WORKTREE_MERGE_PROOF_DEBT write nothing. (5) Tests in worktree/tests.rs: for each of the three uat_stop values, a merge of a standard-lane feature with uat unapproved and with uat approved; a tiny or small lane under close (exempt — clears, does not set the wait); the forced-cleanup-off case under close with both --cleanup and config true; a repeat merge after the wait is set (must still work, grant still present); and the four no-write paths from (4). Follow the existing fixture style in that file; note that a lane fixture file created UNTRACKED hides tracked-file behavior, so create it tracked where the assertion needs it.
done_when: Under uat_stop merge (and the uat_before_merge alias) every merge behavior is byte-identical to today. Under close a merge of a standard or high-risk feature with uat unapproved lands the code, sets the lane's waiting_on to the uat gate mark, writes a next_action naming reload-test-approve-or-fix-and-merge-again, and keeps the worktree even against --cleanup and config true. Under off nothing refuses and today's clear behavior holds. phase is never written, the lane write never turns a merge red, and the up-to-date, conflict, and proof-debt paths write nothing. The worktree suite is green.
notes: Phase 2. Depends on usp-1's crate::uat. Files are disjoint from usp-3 — the two run concurrently.

truths: uat_stop merge, and a repo carrying only the old uat_before_merge key, both behave exactly as bee does today.
Under close the merge no longer refuses WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_PENDING.
Under close with the lane caring and uat unapproved, the merge SETS waiting_on kind gate subject 'uat: <feature>' instead of clearing it.
Under close the next_action names reloading and testing the product, and names both roads out: approve uat, or fix and merge again.
While that wait is live, --cleanup and worktree_cleanup_on_merge true are both ignored and the worktree survives.
A tiny, small, docs, or spike lane under close is exempt and keeps today's clearing behavior.
A merge never writes lane phase; the lane write stays warn-never-fail; up-to-date, conflict, and proof-debt paths write no lane change.
